subject: EdgeScale: MSA/Order Form redlines — output & training rights
messages:
From: Tom Myers <tmyers@edgescale.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, karen.lim@edgescale.com
Date: Mon, 08 Apr 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA draft — output/training carveouts

Hannah — thanks for sending the draft. Our legal team reviewed and pushed back on two items related to model training and downstream productization. Summary: (1) they want an explicit carveout preventing Redwood from using any EdgeScale customer content to further train models if that content is marked as "sensitive" in the Order Form, (2) they requested a limited feedback license for data we share for debugging that expires after 12 months.

We attached a redline of the MSA and a proposed Order Form addendum with suggested checkbox language for sensitive datasets. Can your legal team confirm whether the carveout language is acceptable or whether Redwood requires an alternative workaround (e.g., strict KMS-hold/segregation + audit logs)?

Thanks — Tom
Attachments: EdgeScale_MSA_redline_v3.docx, OrderForm_EdgeScale_Scopes.pdf
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Tom Myers <tmyers@edgescale.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Apr 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA draft — output/training carveouts

Tom — appreciate the quick read and the redlines. Short answers up front: we can accept a per-order "sensitive data opt-out" that prevents training on that dataset, and we can scope a temporary feedback license for operational debugging. A couple things we need to align on: (a) scope and definition of "sensitive" (example list: PII, PHI, GDPR-restricted), (b) operational controls/retention for debug copies, and (c) how this affects our aggregated telemetry (do you want telemetry excluded?).

I'm looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (Customer Success / Ops) to propose precise contract language and an ops plan. If possible, can you ask EdgeScale legal to call out one or two representative dataset examples they consider "sensitive" so we can model the Order Form checkbox?

Next steps I propose: Laura will send proposed MSA redline text by tomorrow; Ben will outline how we can implement a flagged-data flow (KMS keys, retention policy, audit entry points); Jordan and I will schedule a 30-min alignment call for Wednesday to close scope.

Hannah
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Tom Myers <tmyers@edgescale.com>, Karen Lim <karen.lim@edgescale.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2029 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline suggestions — output ownership + training opt-outs

Tom/Karen — Laura from Redwood Legal here. Thanks for the redline. I reviewed the attached MSA and Order Form addendum and propose the following changes to make the contract operationally clear and protect both parties:

1) Training/Model Use: Add an Order Form checkbox labeled "Exclude from model training and improvement". When checked, Redwood shall not use customer-provided content marked as excluded for any model training, fine-tuning, or derivative dataset creation. We propose the clause explicitly excludes (a) aggregated telemetry necessary for service health, and (b) anonymized statistical metrics.

2) Feedback/license for debugging: Add a time-boxed, nonexclusive license limited to debugging and service improvement for a period of 12 months from data receipt. License permits transient storage and personnel access strictly for triage; all debug artifacts must be deleted pursuant to an agreed retention schedule and subject to audit.

3) Output ownership and downstream productization: Clarify that customer retains title to Customer Content and Generated Output. For clarity, add definitions for "Generated Output" and "Customer Content" in the MSA. Add a carveout that prohibits Redwood from asserting ownership over customer-generated prompts or outputs.

4) Evidence & Auditability: If EdgeScale requires separation via customer-managed KMS/HSM, we will accept that as an alternative to training exclusion provided the Order Form documents the key ARN and audit responsibilities.

I've attached a short redline snippet in the body of this email for your team to consider (see below). Happy to jump on a quick call to run through.

-- redline snippet --
MSA §3.5 (Training): "Customer may elect, on a per-order basis, to exclude certain Customer Content from Redwood's use for model training. Redwood will not use Excluded Content for training, fine-tuning, or derivation of models. Aggregated telemetry and anonymized metrics are excluded from this restriction.

MSA §5.2 (Feedback License): "Customer grants Redwood a limited, revocable, nonexclusive license to use feedback and diagnostic data for debugging and service improvement for a period of twelve (12) months, after which such data and derivative artifacts shall be deleted unless Customer consents in writing to further retention."
From: Tom Myers <tmyers@edgescale.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: karen.lim@edgescale.com, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2029 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline suggestions — output ownership + training opt-outs

Laura/Hannah — That aligns with what EdgeScale needs. A couple clarifications from our legal team: (1) they want the deletion requirement for debug artifacts to be "certified within 30 days of request" rather than "deleted pursuant to retention schedule" — can Redwood commit to an attestation? (2) telemetry: they want high-level system telemetry retained by Redwood but raw sample prompts excluded.

Karen (copied) suggests EdgeScale can provide a short list of patterns to classify as "sensitive" (e.g., IDs matching their customer PII pattern, health records, and legal filings) and will include example dataset names in the Order Form.

If Redwood can agree to the 30-day attestation for deletion on-demand, EdgeScale will be comfortable moving forward and we can start the signature loop.

— Tom
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Tom Myers <tmyers@edgescale.com>, Karen Lim <karen.lim@edgescale.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2029 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline suggestions — output ownership + training opt-outs

Tom/Karen — we can accept the 30-day attestation language with a minor tweak to reflect operational realities: Redwood will delete debug artifacts within 30 days of Customer's certified request and provide an attestation of deletion. The attestation will include the deletion date and a summary of artifact types removed (no raw samples included). In cases where deletion is constrained by investigatory holds or regulatory requirements, we will notify Customer and agree on an alternative retention window.

I'll prepare a final redline incorporating (i) the Order Form checkbox text for "Exclude from model training", (ii) the 12-month feedback license with explicit deletion/attestation, and (iii) the output ownership clause. Expect the redline in your inbox by Thursday morning. Once you confirm, Hannah/Jordan can begin the signature loop (DocuSign link to follow).

Best — Laura
Counsel, Redwood Inference
